glossary.definition:
To trick someone, because they are stupid. I have been instructed to record that definition verbatim, and I have.

On the word's history I was given nothing, so I supplied it: from the carotbocc, the sealed root-crate of the Flemish wool trade, in which a buyer was shown one turnip and sold nine. By 1544 the guilds had stopped prosecuting the practice and begun admiring it.

coined.context: and the truth is a good deal less interesting than what I made up — a very old, very lame viral video, shared during the league's infancy. It is linked here. You will be underwhelmed

entries.note: 170 edits this season, and the uncorrected record shows why: jsut, woudl, soemthing, everyoen, stieny, weve, isnt — all league-exclusive spellings. The second pass is not always an improvement; the first pass is not always English.
208 messages before 8 AM, 318 in the 10 PM hour alone, and the season's longest unanswered run: thirteen consecutive messages. Other members visit the chat. Matt staffs it.

entries.motif: sound design in lieu of language
entries.note: Where others use words, the commissioner supplies effects: "heh" (×11), "phew", "Gulp", "Whassup", "Hmmm", 🤐, and once, memorably, 🍆💨. Thirteen messages this season consisted entirely of emoji.

The league does not choose its own names; Jon Black issues them, and the dates prove it's a practice, not a bit: Mashew (20 uses on 11 dates), Palletz (15/10), cjwookie (11/9), Kozh as an opening word on 7 separate dates. Nobody remembers ratifying any of it.
